LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 ESSAY WRITING – EXPOSITORY ESSAY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Essay writing – Expository essay
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.3.1 Essay writing – Expository essay, part of Strand 1 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we organise information logically in writing? 2. Why is it important to understand gender roles in the community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to carry out a research on an issue related to the theme,

2. make notes on their findings,

3. work with peers to brainstorm and write an outline of an expository essay on the theme,

4. create a vocabulary bank using the vocabulary picked,

5. collaborate with peers to sort flashcards with ideas on gender roles in the community,

6. organise the ideas on the gender roles into a coherent sequence,

7. construct paragraphs from the ideas on the cards and sequence them into a meaningful expository essay,

8. edit and review the essay for coherence and effective communication, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to carry out a research on an issue related to the theme,
2. make notes on their findings,
3. work with peers to brainstorm and write an outline of an expository essay on the theme,
4. create a vocabulary bank using the vocabulary picked,
5. collaborate with peers to sort flashcards with ideas on gender roles in the community,
6. organise the ideas on the gender roles into a coherent sequence,
7. construct paragraphs from the ideas on the cards and sequence them into a meaningful expository essay,
8. edit and review the essay for coherence and effective communication, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Essay writing – Expository essay together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced as the learner works with peers to brainstorm and write an outline of an

expository essay on the theme.

• Self-efficacy: This is achieved as the learner shows concerted attention to construct paragraphs from the ideas on the cards

and sequence them into a meaningful expository essay.

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with peers to sort flashcards with ideas on gender roles in the community.

• Love: This is nurtured as the learner displays trustworthiness when editing and reviewing the paragraphs for coherence and

effective communication.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural practices are addressed as the learner discusses gender roles and write paragraphs on the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of expository essay writing to their learning of essays in English and Kiswahili.
